title: Stop, pause and leave the announced direction
stage_label: Separate instructional session · Week 2, Day 2 · individually authored
status_note: Written athletic draft pending independent review. The paused-exit proposal has no current canonical approval. Facility/athlete readiness and precise separate tumbling remain unverified.
brief: Teach an ordinary walking exit in a direction announced before movement, after a complete controlled straight stop and balanced two-second pause. Retain the actually controlled approach. Supported static stance and small unloaded hip, push, pull and brace work follow. The new direction is the learning change; speed, angle, pause, support and strength load are not concurrently progressed.
quality_target: The athlete names the direction, controls the assigned straight stop, holds a balanced 2 s, opens with the exit-side foot and walks into the announced route without a planted-foot twist or rushed cut. Record stop, pause and each direction independently. A planned opportunity, ordinary side gate or supported hold never supplies a completed redirect result.
continuity: Actual OR03 or direct equivalent stopping/stance evidence and OR06 recent impact/hinge/grip response → OR07 announced paused walking exit with retained/reduced support work → OR11 reduces a pause only after repeatability at the retained approach/angle; OR13 checks movement and cue demands independently. Offered dates are not compulsory attendance or readiness evidence.
audience: Ages 12–14 are the reference, not beginners. Every age has explicit standard/compressed D/L and within-age alternatives. Experienced arrivals can demonstrate relevant competencies without repeating all on-ramp visits. Current readiness, history, attention, growth-related changes, sport/tumbling exposure and restrictions determine each domain; older age never supplies a cut or load prerequisite.
readiness: Review actual corresponding stop control before adding an exit. P2 may establish a walking stop; jog-exit needs an actually controlled gentle-jog stop already known from prior/direct equivalent evidence. First jog stopping can use the terminal-stop route alone. Comfortable ordinary walking and turning precede the new exact sequence, but a prior perfect paused exit is not required. Keep actual smaller side-specific stop opportunities, stance holds and hip repetitions from recent work. If OR06 used DBs, today deliberately unloads the hinge; do not label it the same variation. Symptoms/restrictions do not become permission through an L route.
equipment_space: PLANNING ONLY: 15 preparation bays and the five inspected wall stations, three 15 m straight preparation lanes with their own outside returns, plus individually fitting press/row/floor supports from OR03. Exact quantities: five stable wall positions, five incline supports, five benches and manageable single DBs for rows, five mats; breathing needs five leg supports, suspension needs five verified anchors. The main new exit uses ONE dedicated 6 m-wide ×15 m-long shared teaching area centered on the middle lane; the adjacent two approach lanes are CLOSED and incorporated into the protected exit area. Three lanes do not mean three simultaneous exits. Preserve the 15 m straight overrun, with no queue or apparatus ahead. Two 1 m-wide one-way returns are centered at lateral ±4 m, outside the active ±3 m area. Overall main active/return width is9 m plus separate waiting banks, rear paths and coach access. A2 m exit at45 degrees adds about1.414 m laterally and forward. With actual pause lateral position within±0.5 m, the outward path to matching return center is at most3.086 m; planning clearance allowance3.1 m. This is route arithmetic, not a safe-width guarantee or a foot-placement pass quota. Verify body/arm/fall room, exact finish position, surface, overrun and every path. If actual position or path does not fit, stop/reconfigure/defer; do not force the child onto a marker. Separate rear holding banks accept left/right returners without a shared merge. Next athletes feed behind the start boundary through a distinct front staging path. Keep P2’s three independently segregated preparation returns separate from the two main returns: the main area is closed during P2. After the last P2 return is clear, close all three preparation returns and transfer/reconfigure during the opening five-minute main setup; no P2 returner is sent into a merged two-path system. These spaces need not share a footprint. Pre-position both walking and jogging markers; the five-second main gap contains no marker relocation. Provide a separate2 ×3 m observation pad centered approximately6 m left of the main centerline and7 m forward, wholly outside the active fan and return strip, with additional verified access. The0.5 m gap beside a return is not a coach bay. Coach1 must actually see the complete foot/body sequence at either finish. Behind the start, keep independent left/right holding banks inside the outer returns, nominally lateral-3.5 to-0.5 m and0.5 to3.5 m, longitudinal-9.5 to-2 m, each with space for the full group if all return that side. Returners enter only at the rear near-10 m; bank fronts feed toward the central on-deck point near-1 m. No rear arrival crosses the other bank or a front feed. The ordinary staging path is at most8 m behind the start and takes up to10 s under the traffic coach; inspect the actual path and space before using this model. All transfers fit the stated setup windows. All dimensions, equipment, staffing and operating pace are unverified.
coaching_flow: Two qualified coaches: one observes the single complete main movement; the other controls staging, both outside returns and waiting banks. Only one athlete crosses the start at a time. Announce side before release. The next named athlete may spend up to10 s staging behind the start boundary during the prior slot or opening setup; the first athlete stages during19:50–20:00 standard or14:50–15:00 compressed. The inspected staging path is at most8 m, from the selected bank front to on-deck, wholly behind the start; this ordinary transfer never enters the active area or a return path. The prior complete action must clear before release. Returned athletes enter the rear of their side’s holding bank, with no merge across the active area or next-athlete feed. Coach2 may be monitoring up to two returning athletes and one staging athlete. Observe actual sightlines, spacing and path availability; this simultaneous traffic demand is an operating condition, not a staffing guarantee. If both roles cannot be supervised, pause releases. Numbered early opportunities may be delayed or omitted; no hidden walkthrough or make-up work is added.
time_rules: Earliest releases are a model, not a pace requirement. Demonstrations, support/lane checks, marker changes, reset, recovery, water and transitions are included. No cueing interval is filled with extra athlete repetitions. A fault consumes its attempt; no make-up work. If actual logistics overrun, reduce uncompleted later attempts/supporting volume or leave the affected domain unresolved and record why.
preparation_note: Keep the complete reviewed instructional base and concluding hinge/squat observations. Exactly two targets total180 s: P1 retained supported stance/bilateral finish90 s; P2 retained straight walking stop90 s. Unknown-entry P1 is quiet standing. Stationary P2 alternatives remain distinct. The first announced exit is E1 counted instruction, an explicit amendment to the outline preparation purpose, because a full new stop/exit/return cannot be assumed to fit the targeted preparation clock.

exercises.name: Retain supported stance and a balanced finish
exercises.mapping: SPLIT-ISO-SUP plus bilateral orientation; SPLIT-STANCE-HIGH-TEACH when mid-range entry is unqualified
exercises.set_purpose: One short both-lead rehearsal preserves the actual supported stance, then a quiet supported bilateral finish. It prepares position awareness while leaving the new unsupported walking exit for its own counted instruction. The unknown-entry route observes quiet standing only.
exercises.execution: Use the assigned stable wall station. Turn the body so the front-leg-side hand rests lightly on the wall at comfortable waist height; free hand at hip. Lead foot stays whole, rear forefoot on floor. Enter the already qualified comfortable mid-range, left lead then right lead, with3s each; stand fully to switch lead and support hand. Finish in a comfortable bilateral soft-knee base for2s with wall contact, then exit to the adjacent queue. Unknown mid-range entry/exit uses the high-stance branch at a small comfortable knee bend. This is a composite, not one exact source212 exercise.
exercises.cues: Light hand; front foot whole; breathe; stand to switch; two-foot finish.
exercises.errors: Calling both feet on the floor single-leg balance, gripping/leaning heavily into the wall, forcing depth, changing support hand without standing or taking extra practice reps.
exercises.rationale: Retain the useful supported static anchor instead of introducing dynamic split squats or removing support while the exit is new. This rehearsal supplies neither locomotor braking nor unsupported turning competence.
exercises.metadata: Method: one counted position comparison. Tenets: Balance/Body Control/Coordination. Pattern: supported split stance plus bilateral finish. Equipment: five verified wall stations.

standard_D.variant: Split-Squat Isometric Hold — supported-bodyweight-mid-range plus supported bilateral finish — explicit orientation composite
standard_D.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Each lead holds3s. Use light wall contact with the hand on the front-leg side; free hand at hip. No pushing to an end range.
standard_D.notes: One composite cycle:5s entry/setup,3s left-lead hold,5s standing side change,3s right-lead hold,2s return to bilateral base,2s supported soft-knee finish,5s exit to the adjacent queue. exercises.competency: Use the actual comfortable mid-range or higher supported stance, with controlled entry/exit and breathing at that depth. Preserve any smaller recent hold with the explicit cap. If entry is still unknown, P1 is quiet standing; S1 counts the first taught high-stance entries. Neither supported rise nor ordinary step-out proves the new diagonal exit.
exercises.progression: Keep support side/height, contact, stance depth and hold. Explicit 1/2/3-second ceilings apply to both P1 lead holds and S1; never lengthen a recent smaller hold because D is selected. The separate bilateral finish stays 2 s when eligible.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR03 or equivalent supported stance and more recent response → one retained/reduced preparation rehearsal → S1 repeats that actual branch; OR11 retains support while only the independently controlled exit pause may change.

exercises.name: Rehearse the straight walking stop
exercises.mapping: WALK-STOP — proposed walking variant, explicit local lesson; no-travel position alternative separately labeled
exercises.set_purpose: One counted walking stop preserves approach, gradual braking and the two-foot finish. This is the movement component needed before the later exit; the ordinary side gate is traffic clearance, not an assessed announced redirect.
exercises.execution: Start from rest in the marked lane, walk2m with relaxed arms, begin slowing at the2m cue before the marked2.5–3m brake area, and stop with both feet in the3–4m finish. Use several comfortable steps, hold2s, then take ordinary walking steps through the marked side exit beside the finish into that lane’s own return path. This reset occurs after the terminal hold; it is not an athletic cut or timed redirect. The4–8m protected clearance and remaining lane to15m stay unobstructed for an overrun; they are not mandatory P2 walking distance. Do not walk back toward the next athlete inside the active lane.
exercises.cues: See the slow-down space; shorter steps; two-foot finish; hold; walk out.
exercises.errors: Waiting until the finish to brake, reaching for a hard final plant, imposing a left/right plant quota, continuing into a turn or mistaking runoff for extra braking space to aim at.
exercises.rationale: A new whole stop-and-exit lesson plus the full supported stance rehearsal cannot be assumed to fit the 180-second target budget for 15 athletes. Keep the exact walking-stop preparation and teach the first exit inside E1. This explicit outline amendment adds no hidden walkthrough.
exercises.metadata: Method: one predictable approach/stop rehearsal. Tenets: Balance/Coordination/Body Control. No intentional jump event; ordinary walking/braking steps still count.

exercises.competency: Actual comfortable ordinary walking, a controlled gradual stop and conduct are checked within the listed P2 action or direct prior evidence. For walk-exit E1, the actual completed stop must be controlled before adding the new exit. P2 never proves a jogging stop or complete paused redirect. If walking is unavailable, use the explicitly eligible slow-position/standing replacement or defer.
exercises.progression: Hold the actual 2 m walking approach and 3–4 m finish region; do not introduce a faster approach or directional assessment in preparation.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR03 walking/stop record or counted current walking instruction → one straight P2 finish → independently eligible E1 terminal stop or first announced exit. OR11 uses actual separate stop and exit observations.

exercises.name: Stop, pause, then walk into the announced direction
exercises.mapping: PAUSED-EXIT-TEACH new complete proposal; terminal-stop and stationary replacements retain their separate local mappings.
exercises.set_purpose: Every listed attempt teaches or retains a complete controlled stop, balanced pause and ordinary walking exit in an early-announced direction. The first opportunity includes the first actual exit instruction; no separate test precedes it. Standard D uses three opportunities with a 2/1 direction split, compressed D and standard L use one per direction, compressed L one selected direction. Smaller recent count caps omit later opportunities.
exercises.execution: The coach names the athlete and left or right before release. Use the actual controlled walking 2 m or gentle-jog 5 m approach and original gradual braking/finish region. Establish a bilateral stop with soft knees and relaxed arms; hold a balanced 2 s before leaving. Unload and place the exit-side foot in a small opening step toward the announced 45-degree line; the other foot lifts/replants and follows as the body turns with the feet into ordinary walking for 2 m. Do not twist over a fixed planted foot, cross over, force a braking lead foot or accelerate. Finish quietly on two feet for 2 s, then walk outward to that side’s protected return on the coach’s instruction. Ordinary outward clearance is not another assessed exit. A failed stop means no attempted directional exit: keep the protected straight overrun clear, stop the affected sequence and record partial work. The 15 m straight lane end is not a compulsory braking deadline.
exercises.cues: Name the direction first. Stop and balance. Hold two. Open with that side, let the other foot follow. Walk, finish, wait for clearance.
exercises.errors: Leaving before balance, skipping the pause, a late cue, fixed-foot twisting, crossover, forced speed, rushed foot placement, uncontrolled exit/extra recovery step, claiming both directions from one side, or adding an attempt to correct a fault.
exercises.rationale: A full pause separates known braking from the new exit. The exact inspected sources describe terminal stops or immediate cuts; neither is renamed to claim approval for this teaching composite. Directional walking introduces orientation without simultaneously increasing approach output, angle, impact or strength load. Retained supported stance and small full-body support follow after adequate recovery.
exercises.metadata: Method: segmented predictable instruction with full reset. Tenets: Body Control / Balance / Movement Intelligence integrated; Explosiveness component teaches braking and redirection prerequisites. No high-output cut, sprint or jump is prescribed; no performance gain or automatic sport transfer is asserted.

standard_D.variant: Stop, Pause and Announced Walking Exit — proposed composite, retained gentle-jog approach
standard_D.effort_load: Bodyweight; retain the actually controlled gentle jog, about 3/10, with no faster approach. The exit is ordinary walking at about 2/10, with relaxed natural arms; no cutting, sprinting or output contest.
standard_D.notes: One counted complete stop–pause–exit opportunity per set, including faults. The 20 s action and 45 s outside return are planning envelopes, not a forced gait. The 2 s balanced pause precedes the first opening step; a separate quiet 2 s finish follows the 2 m exit. No extra trial, corrective repetition or make-up side.

exercises.competency: Adding an exit requires an actual controlled stop at the corresponding approach, comfortable ordinary walking/turning/standing, conduct and inspected geometry with direct qualified observation. Current counted P2 may establish the walking-stop component; it cannot establish a jogging stop. Jog-exit requires an actually retained controlled gentle-jog stop, not only the ability to jog. No prior successful complete paused exit is required to teach the first one. If the jog stop is new, select its separate terminal-stop lesson; do not teach first jog stopping and first exit together. Stop, pause and each exit direction are recorded separately. Pain, distress, apprehension, restrictions, unsafe traffic, loss of balance, uncontrolled foot/trunk/knee position or inability to follow instruction end the affected attempt. Use only an independently eligible simpler route in a remaining listed opportunity or defer; no replacement trial.
exercises.progression: Keep the actual approach/stop and full 2 s pause while learning the exit. First side is recorded from the actual teaching need; subsequent opportunities alternate. Three means first/opposite/first, two first/opposite, one first only. A missing or unsuitable direction remains unobserved/limited, with no same-day repayment. Actual recent smaller stop counts select the one/two cap. No reduced pause, faster approach, sharper angle, late cue or new loaded strength variant today.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR03 straight-stop/stance and OR06 recent impact/hinge response → held approach plus one explicitly taught announced walking exit → OR11 may blend only an independently repeatable direction at the same geometry by reducing its pause. OR13 still needs independent movement and cue evidence; OR07 attendance supplies neither.

exercises.name: Retain the actual supported static stance
exercises.set_purpose: One combined both-lead supported hold retains knee/hip and trunk control after the exit lesson. It is the knee/unilateral strength role; no additional squat strength set is needed. An unknown-entry branch counts its first high-stance entries within this set.
exercises.execution: At the verified wall, use the same recorded front-leg-side hand at comfortable waist height and free hand at hip. Lead foot whole, rear forefoot on floor. Enter the declared comfortable mid-range with rear knee hovering, hold with normal breathing, stand and switch lead/support hand in10s, repeat, then return to bilateral standing.15s total initial setup/entry and final exit are included. No repeated lowering/rising during a hold. Choose the shallow high-stance adaptation if mid-range entry/exit is unqualified; do not call tall/shallow standing the exact mid-range variant.
exercises.cues: Light support; own this depth; front foot whole; breathe; stand before switching.
exercises.errors: Dropping to an unqualified depth, rear knee resting, rear-foot elevation, full bodyweight leaning through the hand, shaking/straining to finish a timer or double-counting the two leads as two sets.
exercises.rationale: Use the already selected mid-range or higher supported static task. Dynamic repetitions, less support, added load or a longer hold would add a second progression without serving the new exit lesson.
exercises.metadata: Method: instructional isometric, explicit reduction from source2×10–30s/side. Tenets: Strength/Balance/Body Control. Two feet supported; this is not a single-leg balance test.

exercises.competency: Actual comfortable entry, breathing and controlled exit at the assigned depth govern the mid/high branch. Keep the actual front-leg-side hand lightly on the stable wall at a fitting waist height, free hand at hip, whole lead foot and rear forefoot grounded. Unknown entry uses the separate first-high teaching branch with P1 standing; if the first counted entry is unsuitable, end and record partial work. A split hold grants no unsupported exit or dynamic split-squat pass.
exercises.progression: All ages use the explicit 5 s D / 3 s L reference per lead only if compatible with their actual recent hold. The 1/2/3 s ceilings preserve smaller history in either mode. Keep one combined set, support and depth. A capped P1/S1 route never adds holds elsewhere.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR03 supported mid/high or unknown-entry record and current response → one retained/reduced both-lead set → OR11 retains the actual stance while any pause change is separately justified.

exercises.name: Retain a small unloaded hinge after the exit lesson
exercises.set_purpose: One small unloaded hip set keeps the owned hip-back pattern. It deliberately removes dumbbell handling/load when the latest actual OR06 route was loaded, so the new exit and stance observation receive attention. This is a named reduction, not a claim that bodyweight and DB work are the same variant.
exercises.execution: Arms crossed at chest, soft knees, move hips back3s and stand1s through the actual owned range. No wall touch, implement or stretch target is added. First scheduled repetition is the current observation.
exercises.cues: Soft knees; hips back; quiet trunk; stand.
exercises.errors: Turning hinge into a deep squat, rounding for depth, holding breath or automatically repeating OR-02’s possible second set.
exercises.rationale: Arms-crossed bodyweight hinging adds a familiar complementary hip role without another implement lesson or grip demand before rowing. The actual recent repetition count remains the ceiling even if the last set used DBs.
exercises.metadata: Method: one retained practice set. Tenets: Strength/Body Control. Pattern: bilateral hinge; zero external load.

Unsuitable control ends the set or defers the role. No hidden loaded trial is used to decide.
exercises.progression: One set only, 3 s back/1 s stand plus 5 s setup/exit and at least 5 good reps in reserve. Reference D3/4/4 and L2/3/3 are conditional on actual compatible recent counts. Prior two sets reduce to one; load is deliberately zero today.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR06 or equivalent most recent variant, load and completed reps → named unloading or retained bodyweight plus the actual small rep count → later OR10/15 hinge decisions use this actual response and the prior productive record without inventing load history.

timing_narrative:
**Preparation targets,180 s.** Retain OR03's actual short transfers: P1 is90 s,10 s bay-to-wall gathering +5 s reminder, groups of five at15/40/65 s. Default25 s cycle:5 entry +3 left hold +5 standing side/hand change +3 right hold +2 bilateral transition +2 supported bilateral hold +5 station exit. Last finishes90 s. P1 is one brief rehearsal: inter-set rest is not applicable. Actual same-athlete completion-to-P2-start gaps are46–72 s for the full supported cycle; smaller/standing cycles leave longer gaps. No60 s cross-target promise is made, and S1 retains its separately prescribed recovery. Smaller lead holds shorten only those phases; unknown entry uses one10 s quiet-standing cycle in its own bay. P2 is90 s:5 s wall/bay-to-queue gathering +5 s route reminder, three-athlete waves10/22/34/46/58 s. Walking10 s action is2 approach +3 gradual braking +2 bilateral hold +3 ordinary side clearance, then15 s dedicated outside return. Last return ends83 s, leaving7 s. P2 same-lane headway12 s can overlap segregated returns; actual spacing and sightlines must fit. Neither its ordinary side gate nor its return is an announced-exit test. If three walking observations or the paths are not feasible, omit that P2 physical action and use already available direct evidence or E1 terminal-stop instruction; do not fabricate preparation completion.

**Main instruction and geometry change.** Standard15–20 or compressed10–15 includes demonstration, route/side selection, moving waiting athletes behind the start, closing both adjacent lanes and inspecting the shared exit/return area. Coach demonstrations add no athlete attempts. First athlete may stage during the last10 s. Every subsequent athlete stages behind the start for up to10 s, within the prior slot, under the traffic coach; staging does not enter the active area. The new task has20 s active clearance: walk2 approach +3 brake +2 balanced pause +4 opening/walking exit +2 quiet finish +7 ordinary outward clearance; jog3 +3 +2 +4 +2 +6. Both sum20. The exit-side foot opens first, the other lifts/replants and follows. The 4 s exit includes those steps and all2 m of ordinary walking, not an extra2 m after a separate turn. Outward clearance is at most3.1 m to the matching protected return under the stated actual-position condition. Do not force speed to meet an envelope.

**Individual opportunities and return.** Release one central-lane athlete every25 s, offsets0,25,…350 s. A full main round’s last active action ends370 s after round start. The outside return allows45 s total: up to35 m of verified one-way ordinary walking in40 s plus5 s to rejoin the separate side bank. Path length is a ceiling for this model, not a walking quota. First/last effort plus complete return is65 s; the last return ends415 s after round start. Each25 s release leaves5 s between complete20 s active observations. The45 s return at25 s headway may place two athletes on a side path, with20 s overlap; verify actual spacing without passing, shared merges or active crossings. A path or traffic delay stops the next release and removes later uncompleted opportunities if needed.

Standard rounds begin20/27/34 min, compressed15/22 min. D uses all three/two; L uses the first two/one. One/two-count ceilings omit later rounds. Seven-minute same-athlete spacing leaves355 s after the complete20+45 s effort/return, exceeding60 s minimum. Latest full standard D return40:55; compressed D28:55. Remaining time is feedback, water and wall/support setup before45/35 min. It is not extra cutting practice. Terminal-stop replacements use the same20 s shared-area clearance and45 s return allowance; slow-position/standing uses its own10 s no-travel action, while the common releases remain unchanged.

**Strength.** Standard S1 stance45–53:120 s setup, five-athlete groups120/210/300 s; one combined both-lead set, maximum35 s. S2 hip53–58 and S3 push58–63 each get60 s setup and groups60/120/180 s. S4 pull63–69 gets90 s setup and groups90/160/230 s. S5 brace69–75 gets60 s setup and groups60/140/220 s. Compressed S1 stance35–41:90 s setup, groups90/165/240 s. S2 hip41–44 and S3 push44–47 each get45 s setup, groups45/85/125 s. S4 pull47–51:60 s setup, groups60/120/180 s. S5 brace51–55:45 s setup, groups45/100/155 s. Two coaches observe two/three athletes per group; unavailable coverage reduces/defer work. Maximum bouts: stance35 s, unloaded hip21 s, push17 s, both-side row52 s, heel taps26 s. Breathing replacement40 s plus15 s quiet recovery; no overlap of apparatus. Compact row ends232 s in240; breathing recovery ends210 s. Every side-change, setup, equipment move and handoff belongs in these allocations. Preserve each athlete's60 s between supporting roles; waiting is feedback/rest, not an extra circuit.
alternatives:
**Main choices, every age.** Jog-exit D: standard3 ×1 / compressed2 ×1, only with an actually controlled retained gentle-jog stop at the5 m approach,6–8 m braking region and8–10 m finish. Walk-exit in D or L retains2 m walking approach, gradual braking at2.5–3 m and3–4 m finish. All ages D3/2 or L2/1 main opportunities, bodyweight approach about3/10 jog or2/10 walk, exit ordinary2/10 walking. Both hold a balanced2 s before the early-announced45-degree2 m exit and a separate2 s quiet finish;20 s active +45 s return,60 s minimum recovery after both. Every age keeps natural relaxed arms, exit-side opening step/other foot follow, no fixed-foot twist, crossover, forced braking foot, speed increase or external support. Instruction eligibility is not a complete-exit pass.

**Direction and count holds, every age.** Record first side left or right before the start. Three opportunities are first/opposite/first, producing2/1; two are first/opposite, one per direction; one observes first only. A one/two total ceiling takes only the first one/two of that order and never adds work beyond its mode. Use the actual recent compatible stop count, direction readiness and response. A restricted/unobserved other side earns no pass or make-up attempt; use only an eligible retained terminal stop in a remaining listed opportunity or defer. Directions are exit opportunities, not split-stance lead-hold counts.

**Terminal-stop and stationary replacements.** An independently eligible jog-stop remains source155 terminal bilateral stopping, D3/2 or the one/two cap; it can teach a first jog stop from actual easy jogging and controlled walking-stop evidence without adding the new exit. Walk-stop is D3/2,L2/1 or a smaller cap. Both keep the original approach/brake/finish geometry and2 s bilateral hold, then ordinary straight walking through protected4–8 m walking or10–15 m jogging clearance before its outside return. Their enlarged shared-area20 s active envelope includes approach/brake/hold/ordinary walkout, with45 s return and60 s recovery. They grant no diagonal-exit credit. P2 stays one10 s walking action+15 s return. Slow-position alternative P2 one and E1 D3/2,L2/1 or cap:3 s comfortable partial squat lower +2 s bilateral hold +1 s stand +4 s reset, arms comfortably forward, bodyweight easy2/10,at least5RIR,60 s rest, no travel. Quiet standing alternative uses one10 s cycle per opportunity:2 settle +2 quiet bilateral hold +6 standing reset, relaxed arms/unlocked knees, minimal effort,60 s rest, no lowering, travel or split stance. Independent comfortable standing is required; no appropriate action means defer. L never jogs.

**Stance routes, every age.** Keep actual supported mid-range or higher shallow stance: lead-side hand lightly at an individually fitting waist height on stable wall, free hand at hip, whole lead foot/rear forefoot grounded. P1 one25 s composite with3 s each lead,5 s entry,5 s standing side/hand change,2 s bilateral transition,2 s bilateral hold and5 s exit. S1 one combined both-lead set D5 s each or L3 s each,10 s standing side/hand change +15 s setup/entry/final exit,60 s recovery,bodyweight easy2–3/10 with normal breathing. The1/2/3-second caps replace each P1 and S1 lead hold with the smaller of reference and cap; all other setup/side-change/exit phases and the2 s bilateral finish remain. Thus capped S1 totals27/29/31 s. Preserve actual depth and smaller recent holds; D does not automatically turn a recent3 s into5 s. Unknown-entry P1 is the separate10 s quiet-standing cycle. S1 then teaches the first high-stance entries in that same one combined set, with no extra screen; unsuitable entry/exit stops the set and records actual partial work. No mid-range/dynamic/support-removal pass is inferred.

**Hip, every age.** One arms-crossed unloaded hinge set,3 s hips back/1 s stand,5 s setup/exit,at least5RIR and60 s recovery. D reference9–11 one×3;12–14 one×4;15–18 one×4. L9–11 one×2;12–14 and15–18 one×3. Explicit1/2/3-repetition ceilings use min(reference,ceiling) in every age/mode. Choose no more than the actual recent count, including OR06's1/2/3-rep first-DB caps. Unknown history uses the explicitly taught one×2 unloaded set for every age. If the last actual variant was loaded, label today's bodyweight choice a deliberate unloading; no hidden DB test or extra handling is added.

**Familiar upper-body/trunk and replacements.** Default push/row/heel-tap instructions and all age/mode doses are fully listed below. Retain actual suitable support/response, including a more recent smaller dose. Supported breathing replaces S5: every age/mode1 ×4 comfortable breaths, nominal2 s in/3 s out without breath holds or forced depth,20 s setup/exit,40 s total and15 s quiet recovery; calves/heels supported, bilateral comfortable reach, no heel pull/hip lift; five verified leg supports. Qualified suspension pull replaces S4: every age D1 ×4 or L1 ×3 bilateral reps,2 s lower/1 s pull,5 s handling,60 s recovery,at least5RIR; approximately70-degree body angle to floor with actual angle recorded and secure anchors. It needs its own actual grip/body-line/anchor readiness; unsuitable benches do not establish that. Neither replacement adds a set or grants the replaced movement's competency.
workload_narrative:
The complete instructional base remains separately counted. P1 contributes its actual both-lead holds and bilateral finish, or zero split entries on the unknown-entry standing route. P2 contains one straight walking stop or distinct stationary action, with zero assessed diagonal exits. E1 offers D3/2 or L2/1 terminal/exit opportunities before a smaller cap. Exit direction counts are2/1,1/1 or1/0 as assigned, not a bilateral skill pass. Count2 m of deliberate exit travel only on actual selected exit opportunities; approach, gradual braking, ordinary outward clearance and outside return stay separate. Planning return/path ceilings are not completed distance. Exact braking, walking/jogging foot contacts and faults remain unknown until observed. Zero intentional jumps does not mean zero foot contacts or zero jogging aerial time.

Five Strength sets: supported stance is the knee/unilateral role, then unloaded hip, push, pull and brace. No extra squat strength set, load trial, superset or physical finisher is added. Preserve actual recent hold/repetition reductions, including OR06 first-flight impact and first-DB handling/rep response. Supported stance and walking exit load the lower body in different ways; hand support, pressing, rowing and brace still share upper-body demand. Their small counts and generous clock do not guarantee recovery for every athlete.

P1.variant: Split-Squat Isometric Hold — supported-bodyweight-mid-range plus supported bilateral finish — explicit orientation composite
P1.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Each lead holds3s. Use light wall contact with the hand on the front-leg side; free hand at hip. No pushing to an end range.
P1.notes: One composite cycle:5s entry/setup,3s left-lead hold,5s standing side change,3s right-lead hold,2s return to bilateral base,2s supported soft-knee finish,5s exit to the adjacent queue. age_scaling_policy.equal_dose_reason: Short low-effort preparation is not age-based overload. Explicit equal doses across ages are deliberate; task skill, body size, comfortable range and current readiness decide the variant.
age_scaling_policy.readiness_independent_of_age: Experienced younger athletes may use qualified familiar actions; unfamiliar older athletes use instruction. Age never grants flight, rapid descent, floor support, loaded patterns or cue response.

layout_and_timing_assumptions.layout: Three columns of five distinct 3 m × 3 m personal bays: 15 independent working spaces. Five athletes share a lane assignment, never an overlapping crawl corridor.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.additional_space: Unobstructed peripheral coach circulation/access/egress and separately verified start, runoff and return corridors are additional to the 9 m × 15 m bay rectangle. The marked rectangle is not the total facility footprint.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.travel: Standing paths remain in personal bays. Short forward passes are at most 1.6 m; backward/lateral spans 1 m or less except 1.5 m carioca. Individually check full hand-walk/plank footprint before use.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.orientation: All bays face one end. Complete a pass and stop before ordinary walking return within that same bay. No crossing between athletes or concurrent opposite-direction traffic inside a bay.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.coaches: Familiar shared practice: one coach scans A/B and one scans B/C with clear oblique views. Three-wave teaching/checks: both coaches watch one active lane and split five athletes 2/3; other lanes stand. Clear views of all active feet/trunks are required.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.wave_handover: The active lane finishes standing, then the next lane starts on cue. The 2-second change (3 seconds for floor teaching) is a cue change, not relocation. Athletes stay in their own bays.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.equipment: Flat markers, bottles outside active rectangles, clean dry nonslip surface. No partner support, unstable props or unverified anchor is assumed.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.setup_before_clock: Mark/inspect space before class. Readiness/restriction information must be available. First demonstration includes stop cue and immediate comfort check. Unknown restrictions or inability to follow safe directions require individual resolution, never assumed clearance.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.clock_definition: Row time = demonstration + waves × individual execution envelope + explicit wave handovers + reset/transition. The individual envelope includes stated steps, pauses and returns. Shared practice means separate bays, not 15 times one athlete dose.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.tempo_rule: Execution envelopes are estimates for the stated variant, not speed commands. If safe learning/movement needs longer, use contingency, remove optional work or revise the booking. Never rush to validate arithmetic.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.bay_to_target_transition: Base ends at 12:00 full or 7:00 compact with athletes standing in bays. Reserve exactly 180 seconds for exactly two parent-owned target tasks. The parent exemplar defines the split and charges bay-to-start gathering, demonstrations, observed holds, rehearsal, exit and return within those 180 seconds. Use the parent-defined allocation; do not double-charge gathering or hide it before the base ends.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.physical_validation_status: UNVERIFIED: measured space, body fit, sightlines, surface, shared-floor schedule and target corridors have not been observed. Arithmetic does not certify physical feasibility.

teaching_and_competency_policy.full_familiar: Sixteen ordered slots with reminder demonstrations only. SP-11/SP-12 explicitly repeat mastered A-March because exact B/C identities are unverified.
teaching_and_competency_policy.compact_familiar: Eleven slots in original relative order. Omit SP-04, SP-10, SP-11, SP-12, SP-14. Retain floor purpose through the declared stationary-bear modification; hinge and squat remain last.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_full: Eleven recognizable slots in 12 minutes. Easy march replaces jog; optional crossing/flight/B/C complexity is omitted; lunges lose rotation/depth; floor flow becomes knees-down rock-backs; descent is slow; basic march/foot-roll precede observed hinge and partial squat-to-stand. After the easy raise, all actions are demonstrated and observed in three five-athlete waves.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_compact: Same eleven recognizable slots in 7 minutes. Basic walking/stepping/foot-roll can follow the coach in separate bays. Lunge, floor, slow drop, hinge and partial squat remain serialized in three observed five-athlete waves. One hinge and one squat cycle are readiness observations; qualification belongs to subsequent instructional work.
deferred_complexity: Traveling bear crawl and new complete plank/downward-dog flow
Full toe/ankle contact and overhead squat-to-stand range when unavailable
teaching_and_competency_policy.what_deferred_means: Practice the simpler named component in its original place; log performed variant and unfilled demand. Teach additional complexity in a relevant later instructional module. Do not silently pass it, substitute a generic unrelated warm-up or add teaching outside the clock.
teaching_and_competency_policy.partial_competency: Existing evidence can support a familiar variation, independently of age. Preparation completion does not unlock a main family: no-flight lowering is not landing, marching is not running, rock-back is not tumbling, and no throw/cue gate is tested here.
teaching_and_competency_policy.correction_limit: Use visible contingency for actual slower movement or brief corrective repeat and record time/dose/contacts. If essential teaching remains incomplete, mark profile/session REVISE and use the 12-minute instructional base or a justified booking adjustment. Never consume the reserved target time or speed up movement.
teaching_and_competency_policy.optional_reduction_order: For familiar full, remove SP-12 then SP-11, then SP-04/SP-10/SP-14 as readiness/purpose permits. Record omissions and revised clock. Compact/OR already omit these; beyond contingency, further necessary omissions require explicit review rather than an unqualified complete-base claim.

flight_not_qualified_overlay.application: For otherwise familiar athletes whose flight is unqualified, independent of age. This can accompany an independently qualified throw-only main branch, but does not itself authorize throwing or a cue.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-01: Easy march in place for the same 60 seconds full or 50 seconds compact; no flight.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-08: Retain a separately qualified no-flight rapid descent. If unlearned, slow drop squat to stick: 3 × 8-second envelopes, each 2 s lower + 2 s hold + 1 s stand + 3 s reset; no travel. Record changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-10: Omit four A-Skip hop landings; freed time is recovery, not another drill.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-13: Eight alternating no-flight foot-roll actions, four each side: 8 × 2 s + 4 s standing reset = 20 seconds; no travel. Log changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-14: Omit six bilateral pogo landing events; no substitute jump.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.accounting: Subtract omitted flight events and record actual time/contacts. Reduced-impact preparation grants no JUMP-T, REACT-T, throwing, early-release or go/no-go qualification.

records.name: Backpedal
records.purpose: Rehearse controlled backward travel and orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: A related backpedal-to-sprint identity is not this slow preparation task.

records.setup: Face the same end of the room. Mark 1 m behind the start; two short backward steps reach it, then two forward walking steps return. No turn or crossing.
cues: Short steps under you; look forward.
Check the clear space behind you before moving.
common_errors: Long reaching steps and backward lean.
stop_rules: Stop for obstacle, balance loss or pain; use ordinary walking return only when clear.

competency_rule.observe: Controls both backward steps and forward return with balance and stop-cue response.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Lateral shuffle
records.purpose: Access lateral movement with organized feet and controlled orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: This low-intent short shuffle is not reactive cutting.

records.setup: Start centered. Step-close without crossing for 1 m right and 1 m left back to start. Repeat only for the familiar dose.
cues: Stay facing forward; step then close.
Own the stop.
common_errors: Reaching past the bay or racing the return.
stop_rules: Stop if feet collide, boundary control fails or discomfort appears.

competency_rule.observe: Maintains forward orientation and controlled step-close both directions.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog (ordered slot)
records.purpose: Prepare shoulder/wrist support, trunk control, hip movement and floor transitions with low fatigue.

verified_local_names: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog
Inchworm to World’s Greatest Stretch (related legacy flow)
card_mapping_status.limit: Exact composite not established. Stationary limb unloads explicitly replace traveling bear crawl for 15-bay delivery. Knees-down rock-backs are a declared partial-purpose regression, not an exact approved composite. The proposed stationary substitution is specifically four separately mastered single-limb lifts with full replants, not an unspecified weight shift or contralateral crawl.

records.setup: One athlete per dry nonslip 3 m × 3 m bay. Entire floor footprint fits before use. No shared slow-crawl lane or following crawler. Coach checks hand/knee comfort before support. Familiar bear support uses one limb at a time: left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot. A lift means the whole selected hand or foot briefly clears the floor by about 1–2 cm; it is not merely a weight shift. Fully replant and settle before the next limb.
cues: Hands comfortable; breathe with controlled trunk.
Quiet unhurried transitions; soft knees in downward dog.
Keep the trunk quiet; lift one contact only, then fully replant before the next.
Do not lift opposite hand and foot together.
common_errors: Forced straight knees or shoulder range.
Starting the next lift before the previous contact is fully replanted.
Rotating or sagging the trunk to clear the limb.
stop_rules: Stop for wrist/shoulder pain, slipping, trunk-control loss or inadequate footprint.
Use contingency or record incomplete rather than rushing floor entry.

Omit the familiar bear-lift component if any single-limb lift/replant has not already been mastered; use the entire named instructional floor profile and its coaching clock, or record incomplete purpose. No new bear-lift teaching is assumed inside the familiar reminder.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable actual support and floor entry/exit. Rock-back does not pass plank/bear or tumbling support. For familiar bear lifts, each selected contact clears briefly, fully replants, and the trunk remains quiet before the next lift.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Squat-to-stand with overhead reach — concluding check
records.purpose: Observe knee/hip/trunk organization through a comfortable sequence.

card_mapping_status.limit: Source 62 is review state. Familiar prescription follows candidate variant sequential-bilateral-reach-squat-to-stand: standing hinge/contact, comfortable squat, one controlled overhead reach per assigned side, stand/reset. Assigned order is left then right. Current exact dose/profile eligibility remains unverified. The OR thigh-supported partial version remains an explicitly different modification pending variant review.

records.setup: Same three five-athlete observation waves. Comfortable stance/reachable contact points; no forced toe touch or depth. Coaches see feet and trunk. Familiar source-linked sequence assigns LEFT reach and return, then RIGHT reach and return while the opposite hand maintains its comfortable toe/ankle contact; stand only after both reaches. Each reach stays in controlled comfortable range.
cues: Use comfortable range and a stable foot.
Reach without forced rib flare; stand smoothly.
Left reach and return, right reach and return, then stand; do not skip a side.
common_errors: Counting one reach as completion of the familiar sequential-bilateral cycle.
stop_rules: Stop for pain or uncontrolled balance/trunk; use declared partial sequence if comfortable. Longer teaching uses contingency or records incomplete.

workload_and_tumbling_interface.purpose: Finish warm and organized, not tired. Effort about 2/10 and conversational; this is not overload or conditioning.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.full_flight: Four unilateral A-Skip hop landings and six bilateral pogo landing events are explicitly prescribed in the familiar full profile. Timed easy jog and ankling also carry impact; their actual flight/contact detail is recorded instead of fabricated.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.compact_flight: A-Skip/pogo are omitted, but easy jog still has impact and ankling actual contacts remain in the record. Compressed is not automatically impact-free.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.or01_flight: No intentional flight in the first-visit profiles; no landing gate is thereby passed.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.upper_body: Familiar floor work includes a 4-second high plank, brief bear-position support/unloads and downward-dog access. Count wrist/shoulder/trunk demand alongside throwing, pressing, bracing and separate tumbling. Rock-back support is still support.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.tumbling: The separate 30-minute tumbling/Body Control allocation remains unprescribed here. Share actual comfort, support/impact exposure and observations with its coach. Its later load and staffing remain unverified.

reviewable_modifications.reason: Keep purpose with no crossing or long queue travel.

reviewable_modifications.change: Stationary bear-position limb unloads replace traveling bear crawl in the familiar composite.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Five sequential slow crawlers per lane cannot be treated as simultaneous overlapping athletes.
reviewable_modifications.alternative_arithmetic: At 32 seconds per athlete, five serial waves in three parallel lanes require at least 160 seconds of work before demo/clearance, versus 32 seconds with separate bays: 128 seconds extra. Adding that to the complete full clock exceeds 720 seconds without another explicit change.

counting_conventions.primary_repetitions: Always interpret reps_total with count_unit and count_definition. Mixed flow constituents, side counts, foot contacts and timed segments are not interchangeable.
